title: add-telemetry-preflight-checker-and-staged-playbook-executor
author: Maya Chen
description:
Adds a lightweight Telemetry Preflight Checker plus a Staged Playbook Executor to the slo-toolkit. Motivation: incidents often begin with missing/frozen telemetry or missing query access which blocks safe handoff; on-call runbooks need an automated, audited dry-run before executing destructive steps. This PR implements two complementary utilities: (1) preflight/telemetry-check - a non-intrusive probe that validates metric/trace/alert freshness, query ACLs, and sample log access for a target service; (2) executor/staged-runbook - a small stateful runner that can run a playbook in dry-run mode, optionally apply one-step safe actions (notify, annotate, create-incident-draft) and escalate to a controlled real run with an approval token. The description below outlines design, config, usage, and rollout notes.

Design and features: 
- Preflight checks: metric freshness thresholds, trace sampling verification, log tail access, and SLM (synthetic latency measurement) smoke probes. Checks are pluggable and configurable per-service via a YAML policy.
- Staged runbook executor: supports 'dry-run', 'staged' (apply non-destructive actions), and 'execute' modes; keeps an immutable audit log; integrates with incident-bot to attach preflight snapshot to the incident.
- Safety and security: service account usage scoped to read-only queries for preflight; approval tokens are short-lived and auditable via KMS-backed signing; executor never logs secrets.
- Observability: emits preflight.status, preflight.fail_reasons, runbook.stage metrics and attaches a compact snapshot object to incidents (sanitized).
- CLI and API: new CLI commands (sloctl preflight run, sloctl runbook stage, sloctl runbook execute --approve-token <token>), and an HTTP API for programmatic integration with incident-bot.

Files and config: policy schema added in templates/playbook_schema.yaml; example service policy in examples/preflight-config.yaml. Docs and runbook examples in docs/preflight.md. Tests include unit tests and a lightweight end-to-end that runs against a local telemetry simulator. CI runs include lint, unit, and e2e with mocked endpoints.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind SLO_TOOLKIT_PREFLIGHT_ENABLE. Default rollout is opt-in for teams. We will enable a small beta with the SRE team to gather telemetry and tweak thresholds.

Notes: this PR purposefully keeps probes conservative (non-destructive) and places hard limits on request concurrency for the preflight to avoid spamming production telemetry backends.
